title: Ang 1292–1293: Namdev and Ravidas
hook: the temple turned, and the family's work
tomorrow: 1 a.m., boxes everywhere, and a video call from a stranger. who?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ang 1285: the rain ballad ended, burning the praise that makes people forget. Turn the page, and two bhagats close Malar.

Simran's cousin's graduation party: a backyard full of folding chairs and uncles. One of them, holding a paper plate, calls across the table: still driving trucks, Harjit? Still, her dad says, and laughs, and passes the pakoras. The uncle turns to Simran. Good thing you're going to college, beta. Her face goes hot. Her dad built that company from one truck. On ang 1292, a singer gets a far worse version of this. He's thrown out of a temple. And then the temple does something.
screen: `A BACKYARD FULL OF UNCLES.` → `STILL DRIVING TRUCKS?` → `THROWN OUT OF A TEMPLE.`

segments.voice: The singer is Namdev, a bhagat whose hymns are in the Granth. In his Malar hymn, in paraphrase: calling me low, they struck me and drove me out; what do I do now, Father Vitthal? Vitthal is a name of God he loved. And then, the turn. The temple swung around to face Namdev, its back to the ones who drove him out. A building, choosing the singer. On the very next page, ang 1293, Ravidas tells his own family's story without lowering his voice. In paraphrase: my people carried dead cattle around Banaras, every day. And now the leading Brahmins bow before them, because your servant Ravidas has taken refuge in your Name. Two bhagats, two kinds of work the world looked down on. Here's something to tell a friend tonight: the Granth doesn't tidy up where these voices came from. Ravidas names his family's trade himself, and the Gurus kept it in, next to their own hymns. Sikhs hear in it the honor of kirat, honest work: the hands that carry are not lower than the hands that pray. Back at the party, Simran doesn't argue with the uncle. She gets up, fills her dad's plate, and pulls her chair around to sit beside him, her back to the uncle. A small temple, turning.
screen: `NAMDEV: THROWN OUT OF THE TEMPLE.` · `THE TEMPLE TURNS TO FACE HIM.` · `RAVIDAS NAMES HIS FAMILY'S WORK.` · `KIRAT: HONEST WORK, NOT LOWER.` · then, large: `EVERY JOB IS HOLY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one job that keeps your day running and rarely gets thanked: a driver, a cleaner, a cook, someone who carries things. Hold that person in mind for the sit, and with each out-breath, quietly thank them. If you'd like, read ang 1293 first.
Ang 1292. Where Namdev and Ravidas sing in Malar: a temple that turns, and a family's work named without shame.
Your line: every job is holy, and the Granth kept the singers' trades. Day sixteen hundred four, done.

howItsDone: Sikhs sing the bhagats' hymns in kirtan as Gurbani; the Ravidas and Namdev hymns at the end of Malar are found under their names after the Gurus' hymns and the ballad.

notes: 2026-10-15 v3 written: shape story (an uncle sneers at Harjit's trucking at a graduation party; Namdev's temple turns, and Ravidas names his family's work).

Confirm Namdev's Malar hymn on ang 1292 includes 'sood sood kar maar uthaaio, kahaa karau baap beethulaa' and 'pher deeaa dehuraa naame kau pandeean kau pichhvaarlaa'. The script says 'its back to the ones who drove him out' rather than naming the pandits, so no group becomes the foil; confirm that this is fair to the text.
Parents: the hook and teach mention Namdev being struck and driven out, in one plain line.

Confirm Ravidas's Malar hymn on ang 1293: 'meree jaat kutbaandhlaa dhor dhovantaa nitahi baanaarasee aas paasaa; ab bipr pardhaan tihi karahi dandaut tere naam sarnaai ravidaas daasaa'. Rendered as 'the leading Brahmins bow before them' (bipr pardhaan); said without making them a foil. Confirm whether 'them' (his people) or 'him' is right.
'Vitthal is a name of God he loved.: a common description of Namdev's devotion (Vithoba of Pandharpur); confirm or soften to 'a name of God he loved'.
